rule: Constructor / initializer call: `Type#<init>`. Superclass constructor calls (`super(...)`, `: base(...)`, `: this(...)`, PHP `parent::__construct(...)`, Ruby `super` inside `initialize`) → `Parent#<init>`, constructor. Generic/template type arguments are dropped from every ID (`HashSet#<init>`). Overloads share one ID. Companion-object members flatten onto the class. **Implicitly imported names are qualified**: Java/Scala/Groovy `java.lang.String`, Groovy's default imports (`java.util.List`, `groovy.lang.Closure`, …). With exactly one on-demand import (`import a.b.*`), a simple type name that is not in the file's package, not imported singly and not a java.lang type is `a.b.Name` (medium); with more than one such import it stays unqualified, low. Typed receivers (decision A, all statically typed languages and typed PHP/Groovy declarations): a receiver whose type is given by a declaration — local, parameter, field/property (including `$var->prop` / `obj.field` chains whose property has a declared type), catch parameter, for-loop variable, pattern binding — or by `= new T(...)` gives `T#m` (high if defined in the scan, else medium). A type variable resolves to its declared bound (C++: a concept that pins one type, `std::same_as<T>` / `derived_from<T>`; otherwise unconstrained, stays low). An enum constant `E.C` has type `E`.
notes: Constructor definitions are Type#<init>; overloads share one ID, so `this(name, 0)` (the Java form of the listed `: this(...)`) is shop.Special#<init> → shop.Special#<init>, constructor. `super(name)` → shop.Item#<init>. ArrayList and List come from Groovy's default import java.util.*; type arguments are dropped. items is declared List, so add is java.util.List#add (declared type wins over the initializer). ConcurrentHashMap is reachable only through the single explicit on-demand import java.util.concurrent.* (Groovy's default imports, handled separately by the same ruling, do not include that package), so java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap, medium. `this.name = name` / `this.rank = rank` are property assignments, not calls. call_type convention used throughout: a call on a receiver (written, or the implicit this/object of a bare member call) is `method`; a call of a named nested function or an unresolved bare name is `direct`; `new`/super/this constructor calls are `constructor`; calls through function values are `callback`. SPEC lists the call_type values but does not define direct vs method beyond this.
